:::{#exm-convex-on}
#### A function convex on an interval but not on the whole line

Let $f(x) = \minf{x^2, 1}$.

- $f$ is [convex on](#def-convex-on) $[-1, 1]$,
  which is the [closed ball](vector-calculus.qmd#def-closed-ball) of radius $1$ around $0$ and so [convex](#def-convex-set) by @exm-convex-set.
  For $x, y \in [-1, 1]$ and $t \in [0, 1]$, the point $t x + (1 - t) y$ is also in $[-1, 1]$,
  where $f$ agrees with $x^2$,
  so the defining [inequality](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-inequality) of $f$ is the defining inequality of $x^2$,
  which holds by @exm-strictly-convex.
- $f$ is not [convex](algebra-sums.qmd#def-convex-function) on all of $\reals$:
  with $x = 0$, $y = 2$ and $t = \tfrac{1}{2}$,

  $$
  \ba
  f\paren{\tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 0 + \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 2}
  &= f(1)
  && \text{(} \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 0 + \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 2 = 1 \text{)}
  \\
  &= 1,
  && \text{(} \minf{1, 1} = 1 \text{)}
  \ea
  $$

  which is greater than $\tfrac{1}{2} f(0) + \tfrac{1}{2} f(2) = \tfrac{1}{2}$,
  since $f(0) = 0$ and $f(2) = 1$.

In @fig-convex-on, the [chord](algebra-sums.qmd#def-chord) from $0$ to $2$ passes below the [graph](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-graph) at $1$,
while every chord with both ends in $[-1, 1]$ lies on or above it.

{{< include mds/_subfiles/vector-calc/_fig-convex-on.qmd >}}

:::
